chapter: Ben Webster and Jim and Andy's
title: The warm atmosphere; phone from the studios
summary: Women were safe there; studios phoned down for a missing trumpet or sax man.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I certainly hope that someday somebody that's real knowledgeable musicianwise and story-writing wise, would write about that wonderful place, Jim and Andy's, and where your daughter could come and wait for you. There was no placeto meet a chick. It was just a social place where musicians were, very -- a lady wouldn't be molested in there, no matter who she was with.
And everybody in there was very nice. The customers were nice, even the people who were not musicians. I don't know who they were, but they would always be very friendly and it was a very warm place.
It's the kind of place where, you know, you read these stories about some bar in Paris or in Europe
some place, and you don't realize that we had one of our own right here in New York. If we had a writer, as you say, who really knew the whole story, it would make a marvelous story.
Yeah, guys came through there and --
Yeah, after they moved it wasn't the same, of course.
It never was quite the same.
When he died, it was a disaster.
That was the end. He tried to make it the same, but it wasn't. And the old place on 48th Street, between 7th and --
Yeah, it even had a phone up to the studios up there. Yeah, if they had a date, somebody didn't show up, they'd phone down to the bar and say, send up a trumpet player, send up a sax player.
And you could always find one.

Oh, yeah, there'd always be somebody there. Many a date was saved that way. It was a terrible location, because I used to work at A&R a lot, and I used to drink in those days. I don't know how many times I ran up and down those stairs, because the elevator was so bad.
